title: [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois..., pages 650 bis à 787, dont table des matières] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context (pp. 783-786 of the suite to La Longue Marche): G is a topological group acting continuously on a surface X, and I is a finite set of points of X. For each x in I, T_x is the deck group of the germ at x of the universal cover of the punctured neighbourhood. This deck group is pi_1 of a punctured disc, which is Z topologically. G~ is the group of pairs (u, u~), where u is in G and u~ is a lift of the germ of u at the punctures to these germ-universal covers. This gives an extension (128) 1 -> T_I = prod T_x -> G~ -> G -> 1.

The aim is to topologise G~ so that (128) is an exact sequence of topological groups and G~ -> G is a covering. On the previous page he makes two reductions. First, he passes to the finite-index open subgroup acting trivially on I, via the kernel of G -> S_I. Second, he notes that G~ is the fibre product over G of the extensions G~_x, one for each x. So it suffices to treat card I = 1.

This page:
- Choose a fundamental system D_x of neighbourhoods of x that are open discs (131).
- For a disc Delta_{x,0}, take a universal cover of the punctured disc Delta*_{x,0} = Delta_{x,0} \ {x}. It induces the germ-level universal cover D_x^{*~} on D_x^*.
- By continuity of the action, and since u(x) = x, there are a neighbourhood U of 1 in G and an open disc Delta_{x,1} with U x Delta_{x,1} -> Delta_{x,0} (132).
- Then, for fixed u in U, a lift u~ of the germ u_{D_x} to D_x^~ is the same as a map u~_{0,1}: Delta~*_{x,1} -> Delta~*_{x,0} (133) covering u|Delta*_{x,1}: Delta*_{x,1} -> Delta*_{x,0}.
- This holds because Delta*_{x,1} inside Delta*_{x,0} induces an isomorphism on pi_1, so the universal cover restricts to the universal cover. Germ-lifts are then determined by, and determine, lifts on a fixed smaller punctured disc.

The next page completes the step:
- Topologise U~ = preimage of U in G~ by the coarsest topology making two maps continuous: p_1: U~ -> U, and q: (u, u~) -> u~_{0,1} into Cont(Delta~*_{x,1}, Delta~*_{x,0}) with the compact-open topology, together with q composed with inversion.
- Take the image filter of neighbourhoods of 1 as defining a group topology on G~.
- Claim that G~ -> G is a topological covering. Grothendieck writes "J'admets que tout marche".

Purpose: build a topological extension of a transformation group by the 'loop around the puncture' groups. This is the topological analogue of passing from punctures to tangential base points or boundary components. In mapping-class-group terms it is the analogue of 1 -> Z^n -> Gamma_{g, n boundary} -> Gamma_{g,n} -> 1, presumably prepared for the Teichmüller-tower discussion that follows ("Quand X est une surface orientable, connexe...").
errors: No real error. The verification that the filter defines a group topology and that G~ -> G is a covering is explicitly admitted, not proved; it is standard but nontrivial point-set work. Making it rigorous needs, for example, local compactness and local connectedness of the punctured discs, and compatibility of the compact-open topology with composition.

The lift in (133) exists because Delta~*_{x,1} is simply connected. Its compatibility with the germ identification uses that Delta*_{x,1} -> Delta*_{x,0} is a pi_1-isomorphism; this is implicit in the text.

Orientation: for u reversing orientation near x, T_x would not be central in G~. The crossed-out remark about index dividing 2^card I on the previous page suggests he considered restricting to orientation-preserving elements. This page does not address it.

ideas.what: Extension of a topological transformation group G of a surface by the local fundamental groups T_x of punctured neighbourhoods of fixed points, via lifts to germs of universal covers, with a topology making it a covering group
ideas.modern_name: Central extension by boundary/puncture twists (capping sequence); lifting group actions to universal covers of punctured discs or tangential base points
ideas.usually_credited_to: Folklore. The mapping-class version is standard (e.g. Farb-Margalit, the capping/forgetful exact sequences).
ideas.where_published: Possibly touched on in La Longue Marche (1981, circulated) in the tangential base point / Teichmüller tower discussions; not in Esquisse in this form

ideas.what: Reduction to one point via finite-index subgroup acting trivially on I and fibre product of the extensions
ideas.modern_name: Standard reduction / fibre product of extensions

ideas.what: Topology on the extension via compact-open topology on lifts over a smaller disc
ideas.modern_name: Compact-open topology on lifts; covering group of a topological group

deep.surprise_reason: Careful but routine point-set topology for topologising a well-understood extension (puncture vs boundary/twist). The key verification is admitted. Nothing beyond what specialists know.
transcription_corrections: 'Δ_{x,0}^{α} = Δ_{x,0} ∖ {x}' is more likely Δ*_{x,0} = Δ_{x,0} ∖ {x}; likewise 'D_x^{α~} sur D_x^*' should be D_x^{*~} sur D_x^*.
'qui soit [-un-] disques ouverts' -> 'qui soient des disques ouverts'.

The (133) passage should read: 'pour u ∈ U fixé, la donnée des relèvements ũ de u_{D_x} à D_x^~ équivaut à celle d'un relèvement Δ~*_{x,1} → Δ~*_{x,0} compatible avec u|Δ*_{x,1}'. The arrows are between punctured universal covers, and the 'en E' is probably a stray mark or abbreviation.
Final line 'on a' is likely 'on va', continuing onto the next page with 'introduire la top.'
